name: Gluu
abstract: Open-source identity and access management platform from Austin, Texas, built around the Linux Foundation's Janssen Project (Apache 2.0), which implements OAuth 2.0, OpenID Connect, SAML 2.0, FIDO2, SCIM 2.0, and UMA 2.0. Free to self-host; Gluu Flex is the commercial distribution adding a hosted control plane, Cedarling (an embeddable Cedar-based policy decision point for fine-grained ABAC), Agama Lab (a low-code authentication workflow designer), and enterprise support. Historically known as the Gluu Server; increasingly positioned around Zero Trust and AI agent/workload identity.

featureList.description: Core authentication against the configured persistence layer (LDAP, MySQL, PostgreSQL, Couchbase, or Spanner).
Inbound identity from Google, Facebook, Apple, and other providers historically via the Passport.js module; configurable today via Agama or custom interception scripts.
FIDO2/WebAuthn passkey enrollment and authentication via the jans-fido2 component.
No built-in email-OTP authenticator; achievable via a custom Agama flow or person authentication script.
No built-in SMS-OTP passwordless authenticator; achievable via custom Agama flow integrating an SMS provider.
Not documented as a built-in authenticator; would require a custom script.
Gluu requires an identified user or client for authentication; no anonymous/guest session concept.
TOTP one-time password authenticator, enrollable via Gluu Casa self-service portal.
OTP interception script supports both HOTP and TOTP modes.
Legacy FIDO U2F devices supported for migration; new enrollments use FIDO2/WebAuthn.
Achievable via custom person authentication script; no built-in email-code authenticator.
SMS OTP as a second factor achievable via custom script/Agama flow rather than a built-in authenticator.
Not documented as a built-in feature.
Super Gluu is Gluu's free mobile app providing out-of-band push-notification 2FA, backed by FIDO U2F key enrollment.
Context-based/risk-based authentication flows configurable through Agama low-code workflows and interception scripts.
Duo Security interception script available for MFA integration.
ACR (Authentication Context Class Reference) values let relying parties request a stronger authentication method for a given transaction.
SAML 2.0 IdP support via the bundled Shibboleth Identity Provider module.
OAuth 2.0 client credentials grant, plus UMA 2.0 for API resource protection.
Inbound OIDC identity provider federation configurable via Agama or interception scripts.
SAML federation via the Shibboleth IdP module, including third-party SP/IdP metadata exchange.
LDAP is one of the pluggable persistence backends, with direct Active Directory bind supported.
Azure AD/Entra ID federation via generic OIDC or SAML identity provider configuration.
Bulk user import via the SCIM 2.0 API or direct persistence-layer import (LDIF/SQL).
Legacy password hash/credential migration supported via a custom person authentication ("lazy migration") script.
Bulk user export via the SCIM 2.0 API.
SCIM 2.0 PATCH/DELETE operations for bulk update and delete.
SCIM 2.0 PATCH supports upsert-style updates.
Username constraints depend on the configured persistence backend; no universal normalization built in.
Not documented as a bulk import API; MFA devices are typically enrolled per-user via Casa or Super Gluu.
SCIM 2.0 server (RFC 7642/7643/7644) exposes CRUD endpoints for Users and Groups.
Janssen ships a SCIM server; acting as a SCIM client to provision downstream systems is not documented.
Just-in-time user creation on first federated (social/SAML/OIDC) login via interception scripts or Agama flows.
Custom person authentication script pattern validates credentials against a legacy system and migrates the user on first login.
Gluu Casa is a self-service portal for password reset and credential (FIDO2, TOTP, Super Gluu, SMS, X.509) management.
Achievable via custom interception scripts during federated login; no built-in account-linking UI.
User accounts can be disabled via SCIM (active=false) or the admin UI/TUI.
Custom user attributes stored in the configured persistence backend and exposed via SCIM.
Custom client attributes configurable via the Config API/TUI.
Determined by the configured persistence backend; no universal documented limit.
User search via SCIM 2.0 filter queries.
Role-based access via OAuth scopes and Cedarling Cedar policies.
No documented multi-organization/tenant management model; each deployment is effectively single-tenant.
Not documented as a built-in feature; would require a custom Agama flow.
Cedarling is an embeddable Policy Decision Point built on the Rust Cedar engine, supporting attribute-based access control policies.
Cedarling delivers fine-grained authorization decisions in under 50 microseconds, embeddable client- or server-side.
OAuth 2.0 scopes and UMA 2.0 for centralized API/resource access management, a founding use case of the platform.
User data export via the SCIM 2.0 API.
User deletion via SCIM DELETE.
OAuth 2.0 consent screen plus post-authentication consent workflows configurable via Agama.
Self-hosted deployment in any region; Flex hosting supports multiple geographic locations per plan.
Self-hosted via VM installers, Docker, or Helm charts for Kubernetes.
Server and authorization decision logging; retention is operator-configured.
Cedarling decision logs can be connected to ITDR/SIEM platforms for real-time monitoring.
Depends on the configured persistence backend's own encryption-at-rest support; not a built-in Janssen feature.
TLS enforced for all endpoints; mutual TLS supported for client authentication.
Full key management control via self-hosted deployment.
Account lockout and rate-limiting configuration for authentication endpoints.
Rate limiting configurable at the endpoint level; no dedicated IP-reputation engine documented.
Login page and templates are customizable per deployment; no multi-organization branding model.
MFA/ACR policy configurable per client via scopes and interception scripts; not scoped to a multi-org model.
Not documented as a distinct SDK-driven embedded flow beyond redirect-based OIDC.
Login pages, Casa portal, and email templates are fully themeable.
Multi-language login pages and email templates.
Casa provides a prebuilt self-service UI; no separate general-purpose UI component library.
Structured audit/decision logs feed external SIEM/ITDR tools; no built-in analytics dashboard.
jans-client libraries plus Cedarling SDKs (Rust core with WASM, Python, Java, and mobile bindings).
Config REST API, CLI, and Text-based UI (TUI) for server configuration and client management.
Rate limiting configurable per endpoint; no dedicated per-tenant quota system.
Interception scripts (Python/Java via Jython) and Agama low-code flows for custom authentication and authorization logic.
Custom logic is written in Python/Java (interception scripts) or the Agama DSL, not TypeScript/JavaScript.
Self-hosted deployment supports any custom domain.
Janssen CLI and Text-based UI (TUI) for scripted configuration; Helm charts for Kubernetes CI/CD.
Official JanssenProject/terraform-provider-jans manages auth server configuration, clients, scopes, users, and scripts as code.
Pluggable persistence layer supports LDAP, MySQL, PostgreSQL, Couchbase, and Spanner, including hybrid combinations per data category.
Not documented as a first-class feature beyond SIEM/ITDR log streaming.
Full HTML/CSS customization of the hosted login pages.
Configurable SMTP server for outbound notifications.
Custom scopes and claims via dynamic scopes and interception scripts.
Agama Lab provides a drag-and-drop designer for building multi-step, multi-factor authentication workflows without coding.
No general document/identity verification integration documented.
Not a documented feature of the current Janssen/Cedarling stack.
Gluu Flex mints scoped JWTs for both workload and person identity, and Cedarling is positioned for AI agent authorization decisions as part of a Token-Based Access Control (TBAC) model.

The Janssen auth-server (Gluu's open-source successor) runs on Java. Java's own hybrid PQC TLS 1.3 support (JEP 527) only reached JDK 27 early-access builds in 2026 and is not yet GA; even once available it would be a JVM/runtime capability, not a documented Janssen/Gluu vendor feature, and TLS termination is typically handled by an operator-controlled reverse proxy in front of the auth server.

No PQC JWA signing support is shipped. There is one open GitHub feature request in the Janssen Project repo (issue #14253, 'enable post quantum algorithms on AS', milestone 2.6.0), but it has no linked PR, no specified algorithms, and is unimplemented.

The only public roadmap signal is GitHub issue #14253 in JanssenProject/jans, an open, milestone-tagged (2.6.0) feature request to enable post-quantum algorithms on the Auth Server. This is a maintainer-filed backlog item, not a published roadmap document, blog post, or whitepaper; no timeline or algorithm scope has been disclosed.
No public evidence found that the provider supports ML-KEM or HPKE (RFC 9180) for encrypting JWE tokens, SAML assertions, or user secrets.
No public evidence found of post-quantum or hybrid X.509 digital certificate support for mTLS client authentication or federation endpoints.
No public evidence found of NIST SP 800-208 stateful hash-based signature scheme support (LMS/HSS, XMSS).
